title.narrative: Emergency support to protect agricultural, livestock and fisheries livelihoods affected by conflict and COVID-19 in Yemen.

description.narrative: 1 - 7,000 beneficiary fishing families supported by improving their fishing production and increasing production capacity after completing and rehabilitating / building 4 fishing landing sites targeted in the project.​ 2 - 3,000 vulnerable fishing families benefiting from the activity through insurance (3,000 'soft polyethylene' life jackets, 1,000 '450 liter fibre-reinforced plastic' ice boxes - one per household) to improve fishing capacity and conservation. Providing the necessary training for 20 main trainers from the concerned ministry’s staff in the field of good fishing practices to train and educate the beneficiaries in conjunction with the distribution of the inputs to them. The following are for each beneficiary family: (3 liters of natural neem pesticide, 1 sprayer of 16 liters capacity, 2 polyethylene sheets, 1 set of PPE personal protection equipment, 5 homemade collection baskets, 1 set of agricultural tools “axe, shovel, Ma’awal”), and providing the necessary training by 18 main trainers and 50 agricultural extension workers from the relevant ministry in the field of good agricultural practices so that they can provide training and awareness to the beneficiaries in conjunction with the distribution of inputs to them.​4 - 15,000 vulnerable families benefiting from an improvement in production Animal feed through the secured and distributed inputs, which contain the following inputs for each beneficiary family: (150 kg of concentrated animal feed for animals and small ruminants "sheep and goats", 15 kg of local cubes "3 cubes p. Pressed pellets, each weighing 5 kg"), and providing the necessary training for 18 main trainers and 65 animal guides in the field of best practices in animal husbandry to the employees of the concerned ministry so that they can then communicate important information to the beneficiaries in conjunction with distributing the inputs to them.​

1- Improving access to fish landing sites by rehabilitating/constructing and equipping productive infrastructure.​ ​2- Increasing access to basic fishing inputs for vulnerable fishing families​ 3- Increasing the food production capacity of vulnerable agricultural families by providing agricultural inputs. 4 - Increasing animal production for vulnerable families who own livestock through the distribution of local feed and cubes.

A project to improve livelihoods and benefit 34,500 families of farmers, livestock owners and fishermen selected according to mandatory and complementary selection criteria in 14 districts located in 4 Yemeni governorates that were classified between stage 3 to stage 4 in the Integrated Phase Classification (IPC).
